newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech share slide continues on Prague bourse.
newsitem.headline: Czech share slide continues on Prague bourse.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange's bear run showed no signs of easing as Czech shares lost ground for the fourth consecutive session on Friday, led by more disappointing first quarter corporate results.
Utility CEZ lost 14 crowns after reporting lower-than- expected profit for the first three months of the year, helping pull the PX50 index down 0.38 percent to 527.3.
CEZ said net profit for the first three months of the year, calculated according to international accounting standards, eased to 2.84 billion crowns from 3.66 billion for the same period last year.
Company officials blamed the poor results mainly on a drop in demand for energy, which fell by 5.5 percent for the period, year-on-year, as industrial output slowed.
"These results are even worse than we expected," said John Vax, director of capital markets at ING Barings.

"The fall is indicative of a decline of electricity consumption in the industrial sector, which means...the economy is coming to an industrial recession, which is negative for CEZ shares, as well as Komercni Banka, which is quite exposed in that sector," he added.
Komercni shares closed down 20 crowns at 2,166.
On Wednesday Komercni said its first quarter 1997 net profit had fallen to 1.043 billion crowns from 1.348 billion in the same period last year, according to international accounting standards.
According to Czech accounting, Komercni's net profit in the first quarter fell to 0.867 billion crowns from 1.359 billion.
Overall volume was thin with some 697,277 shares changing hands on turnover of 551.26 million crowns. A total of 167 issues rose on the day, while 153 fell and 85 held steady.
Bank IPB, which has been embroiled in a fraud scandal involving two senior managers, was unchanged at 304 crowns after falling heavily on Wednesday.

Analysts said foreign investors were put off by the lack of transparency in the market but that the IPB probe could eventually have a positive impact those most are still waiting for details of the substance of the IPB investigations.
On Tuesday, IPB Director Jiri Tesar and his deputy Libor Prochazka were charged with fraud. The two are being detained pending an investigation into the affair.
